## Check your factorisation {.psf-lesson}

1. Factorise $6x^2-3x-9$ fully on paper.
2. Select the matching answer.

<div class="index-check" role="group" aria-label="Choose the fully factorised expression">

<button type="button" data-choice="a" aria-pressed="false">A. $3(2x^2-x-3)$</button>
<button type="button" data-choice="b" aria-pressed="false">B. $3(x+2)(x-3)$</button>
<button type="button" data-choice="c" aria-pressed="false">C. $3(2x+3)(x-1)$</button>
<button type="button" data-choice="d" aria-pressed="false">D. $3(2x-3)(x+1)$</button>

</div>

<div class="check-feedback" aria-live="polite" aria-atomic="true">
<div data-result="a" hidden>

You took out 3. The quadratic inside still factorises. Find its P and S and try again.

</div>
<div data-result="b" hidden>

Your pair $2,-3$ is correct. Use it to split $-x$ into $2x-3x$, then group. Try again.

</div>
<div data-result="c" hidden>

Expand the inner brackets. Their middle term is $+x$. Which signs give $-x$? Try again.

</div>
<div data-result="d" hidden>

**Correct.** Take out $3$: $3(2x^2-x-3)$. For $P=-6$, $S=-1$, the pairs $(1,-6),(2,-3)$ have sums $-5,-1$. Choose $2,-3$.

$=3(2x^2+2x-3x-3)$

$=3[2x(x+1)-3(x+1)]=3(2x-3)(x+1)$.

</div>
</div>

<button class="reset-check" type="button" hidden>Try again from the start</button>
